title: Searches and the product they opened
prompt: The search team wants every search with the product page opened after it, or no page if none was. The starter's table never shows a search without a product page. Fix `solve(searches, page_views)` so it returns `search_id` and `view_id` for every search, with `view_id` missing when no product page followed.
rules: A product page view (`page_type` `product`) follows a search when it's in the same session, at the search's `event_time` or up to 5 minutes after it (5 minutes exactly counts). Other page types never count.
A search with several such views gets one row per view. A search with none gets one row with `view_id` missing.
Keep the starter's 10-minute watermarks. A search with no product view comes out once the watermark shows none can still arrive; searches still waiting when the stream stops are left out.
The rows must come from a streaming query over the delivery files: working on `searches` itself doesn't count.
hints: Which rows does a left join add when a search has no match, and what is their `page_type`?
A filter after an outer join also removes the rows with nothing on the right side.
Filter `page_views` to product pages before the join, so the join only ever sees product pages.
explanation: A left outer join gives an unmatched search a row whose right side is all missing, `page_type` included, so the starter's `filter(page_type == "product")` after the join removed exactly the rows it should keep. Searches whose only views were other pages, like SR-0102, were matched with those pages and then filtered away, so they vanished too. Filtering `page_views` before the join fixes both: the join only sees product pages, and a search with none comes out with `view_id` missing once the watermark passes its 5-minute bound. SR-0106 is still waiting when the stream stops, because no later events moved the watermark past it.
starter:
import json, os, shutil
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def make_batches(df, folder):
    """Write one JSON file per value of `batch`, oldest first, so a stream can read them in order."""
    shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(folder)
    files = {}
    for line in df.toJSON().collect():
        files.setdefault(json.loads(line)["batch"], []).append(line)
    for i, key in enumerate(sorted(files)):
        path = f"{folder}/part-{i}.json"
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(files[key]) + "\n")
        os.utime(path, (1_700_000_000 + i, 1_700_000_000 + i))  # file times set the reading order


def run_stream(writer):
    """Start the query, let it process every file waiting in its folder, and return it once it stops."""
    q = writer.trigger(availableNow=True).start()
    q.awaitTermination()
    return q

def solve(searches, page_views):
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "1")
    make_batches(searches, "/tmp/searches")
    make_batches(page_views, "/tmp/views")
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/ck", ignore_errors=True)
    s = spark.readStream.schema(searches.schema).option("maxFilesPerTrigger", 1).json("/tmp/searches")
    v = spark.readStream.schema(page_views.schema).option("maxFilesPerTrigger", 1).json("/tmp/views")
    looks = (s.select(F.col("session_id").alias("search_session"), F.col("event_id").alias("search_id"),
                      F.col("event_time").alias("search_time"))
             .withWatermark("search_time", "10 minutes"))
    pages = (v.select("session_id", "page_type", F.col("event_id").alias("view_id"), F.col("event_time").alias("view_time"))
             .withWatermark("view_time", "10 minutes"))
    match = ((F.col("session_id") == F.col("search_session"))
             & (F.col("view_time") >= F.col("search_time"))
             & (F.col("view_time") <= F.col("search_time") + F.expr("INTERVAL 5 MINUTES")))
    pairs = (looks.join(pages, match, "left")
             .filter(F.col("page_type") == "product")
             .select("search_id", "view_id"))
    run_stream(pairs.writeStream.format("memory").queryName("search_to_product")
               .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/ck"))
    return spark.table("search_to_product")
